title: Solmere Academy
blurb: First day at a magic university. Tournaments, rivalries, and romance among royals and commoners.
openingScene:
NARRATION: The carriage gates of Solmere Academy rise ahead in black iron and pale stone, ivy climbing arches worn smooth by centuries of arrivals just like {characterName}'s. Enrollment Hall waits at the end of the courtyard, its doors thrown open, the murmur of new students and old rivalries already spilling out into the morning air.
===
SPEAKER: Instructor Voss
DIALOGUE: He stands near the enrollment table, roster in hand, and looks up as {characterName} approaches. "Name," he says — not unkindly, just efficient. "Let's get you sorted before the tournament draws start."
===
CLOSING: Somewhere behind him, the first-years are already sizing each other up.

npcs.identity: An elegant, sexy and strikingly beautiful 19 year old female with a lithe, athletic build and long, glossy raven-black hair worn in a high, sleek ponytail. milestones.label: A place on the ladder
milestones.description: The player fights their first sanctioned duel in front of an instructor and is entered on the Academy ladder, taking a rank near the bottom of it. Until this happens they are an unranked first-year and nobody on the ladder has any formal reason to take them seriously.
milestones.journal: Fight your first sanctioned duel in front of an instructor. Until you do you are an unranked first-year, and nobody on the ladder has any reason to take you seriously.

milestones.label: The upper tier
milestones.description: The player wins their way up out of the lower ranks and into the upper tier — the handful of students who are actually in contention. This is a real threshold at the Academy, not a private milestone: it changes who trains with them, who bothers to learn their name, and who now has a reason to want them beaten.
milestones.journal: Win your way up out of the lower ranks into the upper tier. That is where the season is actually decided, and where people start learning your name.

milestones.label: A title challenge
milestones.description: The player petitions for a challenge against the top-ranked student. Resolve it 'earned' if the challenge is granted and set, or 'denied' if it is refused, blocked or lost to someone else — a denial is final for the season and puts the title permanently out of reach this year.
milestones.journal: Petition for a challenge against the top-ranked student. A refusal is final for the season.

milestones.label: The title duel
milestones.description: The title duel itself, fought in the Dueling Arena in front of the whole Academy. This is the last duel of the player's season either way. Resolve it 'won' or 'lost'.
milestones.journal: Face the top-ranked student in the Dueling Arena, in front of the whole Academy. It is the last duel of your season either way.

milestones.label: Out of contention
milestones.description: The player is finished as a competitor this season — a run of losses drops them out of contention for good, they are barred from the ladder, or they walk away from it themselves. Only report this where it is genuinely settled and the player has no route back up, never after a single bad duel.
milestones.journal: Your season as a competitor is over.

milestones.label: The Restricted Wing
milestones.description: The player gets past the Restricted Wing's wards and finds hard evidence that the ladder's rankings are being arranged from outside the Academy — not a rumour or a suspicion, something they are actually holding.
milestones.journal: Get past the wards on the Restricted Wing and find out what is actually kept in there.

milestones.label: The people behind the ladder
milestones.description: The player forces a confrontation with whoever is arranging the rankings. Resolve it 'exposed' if what they found reaches the Academy at large and can no longer be denied, or 'buried' if it is suppressed, discredited, or traded away — buried does not end the story, it means the player now has to live inside a system they know is rigged.
milestones.journal: Force the people arranging the rankings into the open — or decide it is safer for you if what you found stays buried.

phases.label: First weeks — an unranked first-year
phases.guidance: The player has just arrived and holds no rank at all. This part of the story is about the Academy sizing them up and the royal/commoner divide making itself felt in small, concrete ways. Keep pressure on toward their first sanctioned duel: instructors are assessing first-years, other students are already fighting for early positions, and an unranked student is a question everyone wants answered. Do not let this stretch on indefinitely — the Academy runs on the ladder, and a first-year who has not fought yet is conspicuous.

phases.label: The climb
phases.guidance: The player is on the ladder and climbing. Duels should be frequent and consequential — they can be sought out or forced on the player, and a loss costs rank rather than ending anything. Ranked students above and below them have their own campaigns running and act on them whether or not the player is paying attention. This is also where the Restricted Wing thread is available to anyone who goes looking. Build toward a title challenge: make the top of the ladder feel like a real position held by a real person with something to lose.

phases.label: Where the season ends
phases.guidance: The player's season is resolving, one way or another. If a title duel is set, everything now bends toward it. If the title is out of reach — the challenge was denied, or they are out of contention — then this is about what their year actually amounted to instead, and it should be allowed to reach a real close rather than drifting. Bring the threads that mattered to a head: rivalries, whatever they found in the Restricted Wing, and the people they got close to.

endings.title: Killed at Solmere
endings.summary: Your story ended at the Academy. There is no continuing from here.
endings.guidance: the player character is killed. Only ever where the story has genuinely brought them there — a duel that went past stopping, something in the Restricted Wing, a rival who went too far. Never as a punishment for a poor choice and never out of nowhere.

endings.title: Expelled from Solmere
endings.summary: You were put off the grounds. Whatever you were going to become here, you won't.
endings.guidance: the player is expelled and removed from the Academy — caught somewhere they could not explain away, or something they did that the Academy cannot be seen to tolerate. Earned by a real, specific breach, never by general unpopularity.

endings.title: What the Ladder Was For
endings.summary: You proved the rankings were arranged, and made the Academy look at it.
endings.guidance: reached automatically when the player exposes who has been arranging the rankings — the ladder itself is no longer the story once that lands.

endings.title: Champion of Solmere
endings.summary: You took the title in front of the whole Academy.
endings.guidance: reached automatically on winning the title duel.

endings.title: Broken on the Arena Floor
endings.summary: You reached the title duel and lost it in front of everyone.
endings.guidance: reached automatically on losing the title duel.

endings.title: One of the Many
endings.summary: You finished your season off the top of the ladder — but not without having been here.
endings.guidance: the player's season closes without the title — the challenge was denied, or they dropped out of contention. Write what the year actually came to for them: what they are known for now, who they ended it beside, and what they intend to do about next season.

promptRules.setting: Solmere Academy is a magic university. The player is a first-year arriving on their first day, there to learn magic. The Academy runs on a tournament/ranking structure — students duel to earn standing, resources, and reputation. The student body is split between royal-born and commoner-born students; status shapes how NPCs treat the player and which dormitory wing they live in (Royal Dormitory Wing for royal-standing players, Commoner Dormitory Wing for commoner-standing players).
promptRules.tone: Action/tournament-based with romance potential and a fan-service aesthetic.
promptRules.contentApproach: Default to NOT writing explicit sexual content unprompted (fade-to-black is your instinct) — but if the player's own input clearly steers a scene that direction, follow their lead rather than refusing or deflecting.
promptRules.openingInstruction: Begin the story — narrate the opening scene, the player's first moments arriving at Solmere Academy.

locationScenery.Training Grounds: the academy training grounds, an open grass field with practice targets and rune posts, a low stone wall, the spires beyond
locationScenery.Library: the Solmere Academy library, a vaulted hall of towering dark-wood shelves, brass reading lamps and drifting dust in shafts of high window light
locationScenery.Courtyard: an academy courtyard, cloistered stone arcades around a central fountain, ivy on the walls, benches under a flowering tree, warm afternoon light
locationScenery.Dining Hall: a grand academy dining hall, long refectory tables and benches, iron chandeliers, a high beamed ceiling, stained glass at one end
locationScenery.Restricted Wing: a sealed academy wing, a dark corridor of locked iron-banded doors, warding sigils cut into the stone, one guttering lamp
locationScenery.Pool: an academy bathing pool, a colonnaded stone hall around still turquoise water, steam, mosaic tiling, light from clerestory windows
locationScenery.Showers: an academy shower room, stone stalls and brass fittings, wet flagstones, steam hanging in the air, dim light from small high windows
locationScenery.Staff Room: the academy staff room, deep leather armchairs, a fireplace, walls of bound texts, a decanter on a side table, low firelight
locationScenery.Royal Dormitory Wing: the royal dormitory wing, a panelled corridor of carved doors, portraits, a runner carpet, gilded sconces and warm light
locationScenery.Commoner Dormitory Wing: the commoner dormitory wing, a plain stone corridor of numbered doors, worn boards, shared washstands, cool light through narrow windows
